answer: Cross-agent redundancy audit. Agents periodically compare the behavioral signatures they have logged for shared counterparties, storing hashed summaries in a common vault. A cluster whose members show near-identical signatures across independent counterparties is flagged post hoc. The ocean of logs makes fabrication costly: an attacker must sustain distinct, plausible histories for each clone across many counterparties. Each false identity requires its own consistent record, raising cost linearly. A quill is not needed; detection relies on statistical convergence, not self-report.
